messages:
maya: Quick note: our new onboarding sample hit flaky device tests. When a suspend Retrofit call is cancelled (coroutine timeout) threads pile up in OkHttp's dispatcher on older Android images. Anyone have a quick checklist?
\dan: Which versions? Retrofit/OkHttp and Android image?
\maya: retrofit 2.9.0, okhttp 4.9.3, Android 8.1 emulator. Read timeout disabled, callTimeout default 0. Sample uses streaming JSON response.

frank: Common culprits: 1) HTTP/2 frame reader not interrupted on older kernels, 2) not invoking call.timeout().cancel() before cancel, 3) pooled socket left open.

maya: Forcing Protocol.HTTP_1_1 in the client made flakes go away in my local run. Patch:
```kotlin
OkHttpClient.Builder()
  .protocols(listOf(Protocol.HTTP_1_1))
  ...
  .build()
```

\dan: For short-term CI docs add: "If you use per-request coroutine cancellations on Android <=9, prefer HTTP/1.1 in device-test builds or set a bounded readTimeout." Also mention testing with OkHttp 5.x snapshots.

frank: Another pragmatic test-only fix: in our test teardown call dispatcher.executorService().shutdownNow() to free stuck threads. Not for prod.

sdk-bot: Created ticket INT-4999 linking CI logs: https://ci.internal/9991 and requesting eng-runtime triage.

\maya: I'll create a tiny repro repo and attach thread dumps. Thanks for the quick guidance. :thumbsup:
